fixed: The dive from the curve of the Earth down to you on the beach flooded the whole picture yellow for about a second and a half: the far Sun, pinned near the frame while it grew millions of pixels wide. It is left out once it is far off the picture.
Halfway down the dive the picture was a bare block of sand beside a block of sea; the sunset beach now comes in a few kilometres up, so the dive lands straight on it.
The low Sun is squashed more (a fifth flatter at the bottom), so the flattening reads at phone size.
notes: One journey from space down the curved beam into your phone; the straight line your eyes assume, the real Sun dashed below the horizon by its own width; 0.5 degrees, +2 MIN, SUNSET includes the 2 minutes, the squashed Sun with BOTTOM lifted more than the top, and the phone screen ending on ALREADY GONE with the real Sun just below.
